items.name: Minecraft
clues: Peaceful and creative by day, quite frightening by night.
Children, their parents and even their teachers. It’s the best-selling video game of all time.
A Swedish programmer released an early version in 2009. Microsoft bought his company in 2014 for $2.5 billion.
You dig for materials and build anything you can imagine, in a world made entirely of cubes.
A film version in 2025 starred Jack Black and was one of the biggest hits of the year.
Its name: digging for treasure, plus making things.

items.name: Pac-Man
clues: Simple, cheerful and slightly stressful: eat or be eaten.
Arcade fans in the 1980s, and now anyone with a retro console.
A Japanese company released it in 1980. Its designer said a pizza with one slice missing gave him the idea for the hero.
You steer round a maze eating dots, while four enemies chase you, until you eat a power pellet and chase them.
The enemies are ghosts called Blinky, Pinky, Inky and Clyde.
A yellow circle with a big mouth. The name comes from “paku-paku”, the Japanese sound for munching.

items.name: The Sims
clues: A doll’s house for adults: there’s no way to win, and nobody seems to mind.
Millions of players who would never call themselves gamers.
It was designed by the man behind a famous city-building game and came out in 2000.
You control little people’s lives: their jobs, homes, friendships and romances.
The characters speak a made-up language and have a green diamond floating above their heads.
Its little people are short for “simulated”, and their language is called Simlish.

items.name: Angry Birds
clues: Simple, satisfying and cartoonishly destructive.
Almost everybody who owned a smartphone around 2010.
A small Finnish studio released it in 2009.
You use a slingshot to fire round, flightless heroes at wobbly towers.
The villains are green pigs who stole some eggs. Films followed in 2016 and 2019.
The heroes have feathers, and they are very, very cross.

items.name: Pokémon
clues: Cute, competitive and a bit obsessive: you have to collect them all.
Children in the late 1990s, and the same people now, as adults, still playing.
It first came out in Japan in 1996, for a handheld console. Its creator had loved collecting insects as a boy.
You catch creatures in small balls, train them and send them to battle other trainers’ creatures.
In 2016, a mobile version sent millions of people walking round parks and streets, staring at their phones.
Short for “pocket monsters”. Its mascot is a yellow electric mouse called Pikachu.

items.name: Super Mario
clues: Bouncy, colourful and impossibly cheerful, with music you can hum after one listen.
Everyone, from small children to their grandparents. Its hero is the face of the company that made it.
The hero first appeared in 1981 in an arcade game about a giant ape, under the name Jumpman.
You run, jump on enemies’ heads, collect coins and try to rescue a princess from a spiky turtle king.
The hero is a plumber with a red cap and a moustache. His taller brother wears green.
Nintendo’s famous plumber, Luigi’s brother.
